newsitem.title: INDIA: High prices dampen Indian rice exports.
newsitem.headline: High prices dampen Indian rice exports.

text.p: Export demand for Indian rice is in decline as buyers turn to lower-priced Pakistani rice, traders said on Thursday.
"Pakistani rice exports are competing very well with Indian rice," Prem Garg, managing director of Sri Lal Mahal Overseas Ltd, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter, told Reuters.
Traders said Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was quoted at $300 per tonne FOB. Ten percent was quoted at $285, 15 percent at $250 and 25 percent at $230 per tonne.
They said the price of Indian rice was currently $10 to $15 higher per tonne compared to Pakistani varieties.
"Therefore the demand for Indian rice at present is lower," Garg said.
Traders said Indian rice exports would pick up once the Pakistani rice stocks were deplenished in another month and a half.
"In another one and half months, Pakistani stocks would be over, so demand for Indian rice would go up," Garg said.
Garg said India has contracted to export around 100,000 tonnes of rice to Sri Lanka, out of which 20,000 tonnes had already been shipped.
"We are also getting a lot of queries from Bangladesh," Garg said.
Traders said India's rice harvest was almost over and a good winter crop was expected.
The Agriculture Ministry expects winter output to be around 71.27 million tonnes.
India harvests two rice crops every year, with the bulk of the output from the winter crop. Sowing for the winter crop begins in July and the harvest starts In October.
